title: If BYU isn't sweating Oregon and Ohio State in CFP rankings, it should be
text:
Oregon, Ohio State and the latest threat to BYU’s CFP dreams 🏈 Draft. Trade. Win.  BYU beat Notre Dame, but will the CFP committee respect that on selection day, or fall in love with Oregon and Ohio State?
 Blake Toppmeyer USA TODAY Nov. 18, 2026, 5:40 a.m. ET Hear this story The selection committee’s fixing to do it again, aren’t they?
 Sure as the day is long, they’re moving into position to stiff Brigham Young .
 You think they won’t? They did it last year. They did it in 2024. They’ll do it again.
 If you listen to the SEC’s propaganda machine, you’d think the committee ranks teams purely off record. If you monitored BYU at all the past two seasons, you’d know the record-trumps-all narrative rings false.
 The committee rejected 11-2 BYU last year, even though its only two losses came against playoff-bound Texas Tech. It omitted 10-2 BYU from the bubble conversation entirely in 2024, while Alabama, Mississippi and South Carolina howled they deserved a spot at 9-3.
 So, what’s the committee going to do this December when BYU finishes 10-2 but doesn’t snag the Big 12’s automatic bid?
 We’ve seen this film before, and the Cougars won’t like the ending.
 All you need to do is look at Oregon and Ohio State charging up the rankings to understand why BYU must be sweating bullets.
 Up, up, up, the three-loss Ducks and Buckeyes climb to Nos. 13 and 14. BYU remains stuck on No. 10, despite its signature win against Notre Dame, despite one of its two losses coming against undefeated Utah on the road.
 Why Oregon, Ohio State are a threat to BYU in CFP rankings
 How long until the committee says, We respect that BYU beat the Irish, but we just can’t ignore Oregon’s strength of schedule. 
 Or, You know, Luke Fahey is improving, and Ohio State did beat Indiana, so we decided to catapult the Buckeyes into the bracket. 
 Who am I kidding, the committee probably won’t even provide that level of detail while slipping into old habits and giving BYU the shaft.
 Opinion: Clemson football is one big joke, and Dabo Swinney must be in on it Bama bias: CFP committee’s Alabama obsession has turned its rankings into a farce Selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek explained that BYU’s win against Notre Dame is keeping the Cougars (8-2) one spot ahead of 9-1 Wake Forest, but I’m thinking the Demon Deacons aren’t as much of a threat to BYU as Oregon and Ohio State are.
 --> “The strength of schedule for Oregon is nine. For Ohio State, 16,” Yurachek said, while explaining the Big Ten teams’ rankings rise.
 Yurachek said the committee sees some separation between the top 12 teams and No. 13 Oregon, but the committee isn't held to its week-by-week rankings precedent. As we witnessed last year, the committee starts from scratch on Selection Sunday and cooks up whatever logic it deems necessary to justify selection of the at-large teams it desires for the bracket.
 BYU won’t get much opportunity to improve its resume between now and then. In fact, its strength of schedule is projected to slip after it finishes at Kansas (4-6) and against Cincinnati (5-5). Oregon and Ohio State are lying like snakes in the grass, just waiting for the committee to make the Big 12 a one-bid league once again.
 Can BYU's win against Notre Dame carry it across finish line?
 Unlike the past two seasons, we know this BYU squad could beat a playoff team. It already has. This is shaping up as Kalani Sitake’s best team yet. BYU’s win against Notre Dame looks better, every time the Irish smash another opponent.
 Put aside the conference logo, and you’ll see BYU plays at an SEC or Big Ten level at the lines of scrimmage. Its defense typically delivers, and LJ Martin’s return to the backfield from injury should boost the offense.
 The Cougars are short on style points, but they keep winning. They’re 29-6 since the start of 2024, and although past seasons shouldn’t carry much weight on current rankings, no team in America would have more cause for a gripe on Selection Sunday than the Cougars if they finish 10-2 and get left out of the bracket once again.
 Lost in the midst of the Notre Dame-Miami controversy last year was the committee’s snub of BYU. The Cougars sat on the 11-seed line for three straight weeks down the final runway, unable to climb an inch, before losing to Texas Tech in the Big 12 championship, while Miami sat at home.
 And, presto!
 Miami moved up two spots and zipped into the bracket, BYU got shipped to the Pop-Tarts Bowl, took its medicine, and finished 11-2, and Notre Dame quit the season.
 If Miami can climb two spots and leapfrog BYU while sitting at home, you think the committee wouldn’t consider catapulting Oregon or Ohio State into the bracket at the Cougars’ expense if those Big Ten teams reach 9-3?
 You’ve heard the tired narrative that the committee ranks teams based purely off record, and Georgia being No. 1 ahead of undefeated Utah and UCLA should tell you that’s a lie. For more proof that the committee doesn’t simply bend the knee to a team’s record, see two-loss Alabama ranked at No. 3 .
 Or, call the Cougars to the witness stand. If BYU wins its next two games, it’ll have 31 wins the past three seasons, and how many playoff bids will it have to show for it?
 So far, it’s stuck on zero. If Oregon and Ohio State gain a little more shine these next two weeks, it could stay that way.
